proposals.before: Emperor Wu received him in audience. Andou asked permission to return north and raise rebellion along the Yellow River and in Shaanxi, rallying loyal partisans.
proposals.after: Emperor Wen received him in audience. Andou asked permission to return north and raise rebellion along the Yellow River and in Shaanxi, rallying loyal partisans.
proposals.reason: Chinese 太祖 in Songshu denotes Emperor Wen (太祖文皇帝 Liu Yilong), not Emperor Wu (高祖). The audience follows Yuanjia 21 events under Emperor Wen.

proposals.before: The Founding Emperor received him in audience; [Andou] asked to return north to stir up trouble in the He and Shaanxi regions and gather loyal followers.
proposals.after: The Grand Ancestor (Taizu) received him in audience; [Andou] asked to return north to stir up trouble in the He and Shaanxi regions and gather loyal followers.
proposals.reason: Literal 'Founding Emperor' misrenders 太祖; Songshu temple name 太祖 is Emperor Wen, not the founding Emperor Wu (高祖).

proposals.before: Shuang sent his general Zheng Dexuan to garrison Great Xian. Dexuan dispatched his vanguard Yang Hu with light troops toward Liyang.
proposals.after: Shuang sent his general Zheng Dexuan to garrison Great Xian. Dexuan dispatched his vanguard Yang Huyu with light troops toward Liyang.
proposals.reason: Chinese 楊胡與 is one personal name (shortened 胡與 in the next sentence); rendering it as Yang Hu drops the final 與.

proposals.before: Andou sent Zong Yue and Liyang Administrator Cheng Tianzuo to intercept and rout them, beheading Yang Hu and his second-in-command.
proposals.after: Andou sent Zong Yue and Liyang Administrator Cheng Tianzuo to intercept and rout them, beheading Hu Yu and his second-in-command.
proposals.reason: Chinese 斬胡與 matches the short form of 楊胡與, not Yang Hu; align with the Chinese short name.

proposals.before: Earlier, Andou's nephew by marriage Suo'er had served during the Jinghe era of Emperor Qianfei as vanguard general and direct attendant, joined in the slaughter of the princes and high ministers, and was enfeoffed as Baron of Wu'an county with a fief of three hundred households.
proposals.after: Earlier, Andou's brother's son Suo'er had served during the Jinghe era of Emperor Qianfei as vanguard general and direct attendant, joined in the slaughter of the princes and high ministers, and was enfeoffed as Baron of Wu'an county with a fief of three hundred households.
proposals.reason: Chinese 從子 means a brother's son (agnatic nephew), not a nephew by marriage.

proposals.before: Suo'er had Lingsun persuade Chan to surrender. Once Chan submitted, Suo'er seized both men and had them killed.
proposals.after: Suo'er had Lingsun persuade Chan to surrender. Once Chan had submitted, Suo'er seized both men and had them killed.
proposals.reason: Awkward English "Once Chan submitted" reads like a fused name; keep Chan as the person name Shen Chan.

proposals.before: Emperor Ming sent the Prince of Qi north at the head of an army including Forward General Zhang Yong, General Who Pacifies the North Yuan Shanbao, Wang Kuan, Supernumerary Attendant Cavalier Zhang Zhenzhen, Xiao Shunzhi, General of the Dragon Cavalry Zhang Jihe, Huang Wenyu, and others.
proposals.after: Emperor Ming sent the Prince of Qi north at the head of an army including Forward General Zhang Yong, Ningshuo General Yuan Shanbao, Wang Kuan, Supernumerary Attendant Cavalier Zhang Zhenzhen, Xiao Shunzhi, General of the Dragon Cavalry Zhang Jihe, Huang Wenyu, and others.
proposals.reason: English fuses the Ningshuo/General Who Pacifies the North title with personal name as "North Yuan Shanbao".

proposals.before: Shen Wenxiu, whose courtesy name was Zhongyuan, came from Wukang in Wuxing commandery and was a disciple of Minister of Works Shen Qingzhi.
proposals.after: Shen Wenxiu, whose courtesy name was Zhongyuan, came from Wukang in Wuxing commandery and was a disciple of Minister of Minister of Works Shen Qingzhi.
proposals.reason: English drops 司空 as a fused "Works Shen Qingzhi"; restore Minister of Works.

proposals.before: In the eighth month of the second year of Taishi Xunyang was pacified. Emperor Ming sent Ministerial Clerk for Revenue Cui Yuansun to reward the loyalist armies. He was killed in defeat alongside Senghao and was posthumously enfeoffed as General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Jizhou.
proposals.after: In the eighth month of the second year of In the eighth month of the second year of Taishi, Xunyang was pacified. Emperor Ming sent Ministerial Clerk for Revenue Cui Yuansun to reward the loyalist armies. He was killed in defeat alongside Senghao and was posthumously enfeoffed as General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Jizhou.
proposals.reason: English fuses reign-name Taishi with place Xunyang as a false personal name.

decisions.reason: In the Songshu, Taizu is Liu Yilong, Emperor Wen; the surrounding Yuanjia chronology confirms that he, not Emperor Wu, received Xue Andou.
太祖 is the temple name Taizu and refers here to Emperor Wen. 'Founding Emperor' incorrectly points to Emperor Wu, whose temple name is Gaozu.
The following sentence shortens 楊胡與 to 胡與, confirming that the full personal name is Yang Huyu rather than Yang Hu.
胡與 is the shortened form of Yang Huyu's name, not Yang Hu.

decisions.after: Earlier, Andou's agnatic nephew Suo'er had served during the Jinghe era of Emperor Qianfei as vanguard general and direct attendant, joined in the slaughter of the princes and high ministers, and was enfeoffed as Baron of Wu'an county with a fief of three hundred households.
decisions.reason: 從子 denotes a nephew in the paternal line, not a nephew by marriage. 'Agnatic nephew' preserves the relationship without over-specifying which brother was his father.
'Once Chan submitted' is grammatical English, and Chan is already introduced unambiguously as a person. The proposed pluperfect adds no source-level correction.
'General Who Pacifies the North Yuan Shanbao' follows the book's established title-name syntax and accurately translates 寧朔將軍垣山寶. It is not a fused personal name.

decisions.after: Shen Wenxiu, whose courtesy name was Zhongyuan, came from Wukang in Wuxing commandery and was a son of Minister of Works Shen Qingzhi's younger brother.
decisions.reason: Here 弟子 is a kinship expression: Wenxiu was the son of Qingzhi's younger brother, not Qingzhi's disciple. The proposal's doubled title does not fix the real error.

decisions.after: In the eighth month of the second year of Taishi, Xunyang was pacified. Emperor Ming sent Cui Yuansun, a ministerial clerk in the Revenue Bureau, to commend the loyalist armies. He accompanied Senghao, was defeated in battle, and was killed; he was posthumously appointed General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Jizhou.
decisions.reason: A comma must separate the Taishi date from Xunyang. The revision also renders 隨僧皓戰敗見殺 in sequence and 追贈 as a posthumous appointment rather than an enfeoffment.
